$$
\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{Total distance traveled}}{\text{Total time taken}}
$$

These coordinates are in the form $(\text{time}, \text{distance})$, with the x-axis representing **time** and the y-axis representing **distance** from the starting point (the origin, labeled as $O$).

Each student’s dot corresponds to their **position at a specific time**, which we can interpret as the **end of their run**. Thus, we can treat each student’s run as starting at time 0 and ending at the given time, with the given distance. This allows us to compute their average speed as:

$$
\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$
